great_alaskan_mystery_all: The obsessive scientist Dr. Miller is working on a matter-transmitter invention called the Paratron; a conspiratorial team of spies and no-goods pursue him to Alaska, trying to steal the device.

rv: Definitely among the best serials. Plot goes on and on, with lots of contrived events, but that's a serial. Acting and dialog are solid and believable. The sci-fi stuff is good. Death ray presages the laser, doesn't violate any laws of physics. Best of all, it makes a noise just like Dr Who's Tardis!

I enjoyed the serie a lot and was a bit dissapointed at the missing 13th part. I decided to do a search on Google and the missing part is in the Google Video library. Just do a search for The Great Alaskan Mystery. Enjoy, Michel Tremblay

HamiltonAndJeffersonOnDemocracy: In The sixth and final film in Bernard Wilets's Man and the State series is a dramatization of the controversy between Alexander Hamilton and Thomas Jefferson as the two historical figures debate various crises in American history. They are raised from the dead, awaken, debate the Civil War, the Great Depression, and Vietnam, then are returned to their deaths. Filmmaker Bernard Wilets shown briefly on camera, sitting to the right of the camera, wearing a cap.

rv: Rarely do we see anything currently being created done so well. Yes, at times it is goofy. But not in such a way that will distract modern students from appreciating, enjoying and, above all, learning from the film. Its strength lies in showing how such two diametrically opposed men could both deeply care about the same thing in different ways and yet compromise and respect each other. A desperately needed lesson in the 114th Congress. I look forward to sharing this with my students.

0831_Glacier_International_Park_15_42_10: Glacier National Park, Montana, in 1930s tourist footage: a family packs the Ford, mountain roads and the park's hotels.

rv: The Smell Will Linger in Your Nostrils

Lovely, well-composed footage of the natural beauty of the Rockies is the highlight of this travelogue. Colour would be nice, but a black-and-white version is more than acceptable (though narration about the bluest skies isn't quite as effective in b&w). The audience is reminded the Blackfoot have lived in the area for untold generations, and there's a scene featuring traditional native dancing. There's also a reminder that "the modern automobile" can take you there over 900 miles of good road. The word "Ford" isn't mentioned by the narrator, but the credits reveal that's who sponsored this…

Lovely and simple film telling us about all the wonders that can be had at Glacier National Park in Montana. There are films on here that spend 30 minutes or more on park tourism, but this compact film does it all in 8 minutes and is perfectly fine. Very nice cinematography here.

KidTwist: In this episode of the Witness, Peter Falk reprises the role that netted in Oscar Nomination as Abe "Kid Twist" Reles, an infamous 1930s Hitman associated with Murder Incorporated, as he testifies before a fictional crime committee. Includes commercials. Air Date: December 22, 1960 (Episode 12)

rv: I can see the educational purpose of the Witness series. I value the fact that Mr Falk has played Mr Reles once again, and in good fashion too. I enjoyed the humour value of the episode. I immersly love the 'Murder Inc.' movie and I must say this Witness piece clearly, plainly and strictly corresponds with it. I guess it's best to watch Murder first, though, as it is a masterpiece of its own and then saviour some more here - as a form of extra feature.

To comment on another user's comment: The name "Kid Twist" was not given to the "character" of Abe Reles. That was his nickname, although he was not the first hood to carry that monicker, granted. But Abe Reles was a real person--not a character invented by the writers and producers of this show, as the commenter seemed to imply. That said, the quality of this video is very bad, as has been stated in other reviews. But I watched this installment of The Witness here on Internet Archives because I am a fan of Peter Falk, and I cannot seem to find this episode anywhere else, so, under the…

series:are-you-being-served-1972: This comedy series, which follows the exploits of employees at London's Grace Brothers department store, is full of sexual innuendo, slapstick, visual gags and double entendres. Many of the show's characters are based on stereotypes, including the effeminate Mr. Humphries and the rich-but-stingy store owner.
